text:
Jonas Weber: Dropping early results from the baseline vs quantized runner. Main question: what regression threshold are we ok with for tool-calling + JSON-mode outputs for the library?

Jonas Weber: tl;dr int8 looks fine on general chat + summarization. int4 is where the structured outputs get spicy.

Olivia Grant: linking the sheet view I exported from eval harness run `qhq-2024-11-05a` (internal): https://drive.google.com/.../quantization_profile_eval_results_sheet

Olivia Grant: quick numbers (Llama-3.1-70B-ish workload, 5 prompt sets, ~2k prompts total)
```
Baseline JSON valid: 99.62%
INT8 JSON valid:     99.55%   (-0.07pp)
INT4 JSON valid:     98.83%   (-0.79pp)

Baseline tool-call success: 98.91%
INT8 tool-call success:     98.87%   (-0.04pp)
INT4 tool-call success:     97.60%   (-1.31pp)

Schema compliance (args):
Baseline: 97.8%
INT8:     97.7%  (-0.1pp)
INT4:     96.1%  (-1.7pp)
```

Selene Huang: -0.79pp JSON validity is not “spicy”, it’s “we will get paged” lol

Selene Huang: for context, most customer JSON-mode routes are essentially strict parsers. If we go below 99.5% valid we’ll break workflows.

Arjun Desai: agree we shouldn’t ship int4 broadly, but can we treat tool/JSON prompt sets as “gated” and allow int4 on routes that don’t use tool calling?

Jonas Weber: yes route-level scope is the whole point, but we still need publish gates. If the profile is in the library, someone will turn it on for the wrong route eventually.

Karthik Iyer: +1. we need a clear acceptance rule for “structured outputs” as a category. Otherwise every profile review becomes a debate.

Nikhil Sharma: from Hosted API POV: I’d really like the rule to be simple for docs: “don’t use int4 on JSON/tool routes” is fine *if* we can reliably detect / warn.

Mateo Alvarez: runtime can tag execution mode, but we can’t reliably know if your prompt expects strict JSON unless you’re using our JSON mode / tool calling APIs. If customer is “DIY JSON in prompt”, we have no signal.

Selene Huang: exactly. so the gate should assume worst case: if the model is marketed as supporting JSON-mode/tool-calling, quant profile can’t degrade it beyond a very small delta.

Dr. Maya Srinivasan: what’s the actual customer risk tolerance here? is a 0.1pp drop acceptable if we’re saving 30% cost? (asking genuinely)

Sana Farid: I pulled recent production stats (approx) for top JSON-mode routes: failure budgets are tight. Many teams are already at 0.2–0.4% parse failures due to prompt bugs / model drift. If we add another ~0.8% we’re doubling their failure rate.

Aditya Rao: Optimize perspective: if we want adoption, we need to be conservative. People will try it once; if it breaks JSON they won’t come back.

Jonas Weber: proposal:
- Define “structured outputs” gate on our quant prompt sets (tool-calling, json-mode, schema args)
- Set default acceptance threshold for publish:
  - JSON valid rate regression <= 0.10pp AND absolute JSON valid >= 99.50%
  - tool-call success regression <= 0.25pp AND absolute tool-call success >= 98.5%
  - schema compliance regression <= 0.25pp
- Exceptions require Maya+Selene signoff + profile metadata flag `unsafe_for_structured_outputs=true` + docs warning

Arjun Desai: I’m ok with those thresholds for “safe” profiles. But I want an on-ramp for int4 to exist.

Selene Huang: I’m fine with an “unsafe” tier as long as it’s loud. Like, in Console it should say “Not recommended for JSON/tool routes” and default-off.

Nikhil Sharma: +1, and API should reject enabling unsafe profiles on routes with `response_format=json_schema` / tool calling enabled (unless explicit override).

Mateo Alvarez: on the runtime side, we can surface a compatibility + safety check back to control plane. Something like: if route config includes structured-output features, only allow profiles with `structured_outputs=pass`.

Olivia Grant: note: these deltas are with n~400 structured prompts (subset). we should confirm significance; the int4 drop is definitely real though (it’s not a flake).

Jonas Weber: yeah, the bootstrap CI on JSON validity for int8 overlaps 0 for delta; for int4 it’s clearly negative.

Karthik Iyer: can we add one more metric: “strict JSON roundtrip parse + schema validate” vs just syntactic validity? syntactic valid but wrong keys is still a break.

Olivia Grant: we already have schema compliance, but it’s not end-to-end for every prompt set. I can expand the tool-calling set to validate args JSON schema strictly.

Selene Huang: also: please track “hallucinated tool name” separately. That’s been a real customer pain point.

Jonas Weber: 👍 will update eval harness report fields: `tool_name_match_rate`, `args_schema_valid_rate`, `json_valid_rate`.

Dr. Maya Srinivasan: I like the “safe vs unsafe” split. Please make sure unsafe profiles have hard guardrails (canary-only?)

Aditya Rao: could we require unsafe profiles to have canary max 5% by default and no auto-expand? (force manual)

Mateo Alvarez: control plane can set defaults + enforce max canary for unsafe. Rafael/Sean will probably want that anyway.

Arjun Desai: ok. action items:
1) Jonas/Olivia: codify thresholds + add tool_name_match + strict schema checks.
2) Selene/Sana: confirm “absolute” floors for JSON/tool metrics align with prod expectations.
3) Aditya/Nikhil: decide UX/API wording + enforcement for “unsafe for structured outputs”.

Selene Huang: also, please add a rule in the profile review checklist: any profile with structured regression > 0.25pp must be marked unsafe, no exceptions.

Jonas Weber: ack. I’ll draft it into the acceptance thresholds doc + link in the next profile publish PR.

Nikhil Sharma: if we do this, I’m comfortable telling customers: int8 is generally safe; int4 is route-specific and not for JSON/tool routes.

Dr. Maya Srinivasan: sounds good. let’s not block int8 library launch on int4 drama.

Olivia Grant: I’ll rerun with the expanded structured set tonight and post updated numbers. :thumbsup:

Jonas Weber: thanks all. closing loop once updated run is in.
